title: Harness prompt assembly buries the operator task under directive preamble + memory-as-user-turn — smaller models conclude "no task provided"
wanted_capability: The dispatched prompt should be unmistakably demarcated as THE task, not appended unmarked after stacked directives. Observed (session 7476e678, vibebh/mistral-medium-3.5, openai-chat): first user turn = 2,845 chars of [scope]+[recall before acting]+[task shape]+[completion contract]+[milestone reporting] with the operator's one-line instruction as the bare last line; second user turn = 15,434 chars of rendered provider memory; the model answered "the user hasn't actually provided a task yet" and wandered. The same model follows the same instruction fine in its native CLI (clean prompt), so this is harness prompt assembly, not model capability. Candidate fixes (design decision): (a) explicit [task] demarcation or task-first ordering with directives after; (b) move standing directives to the system message on transports that support it (openai-chat allows a leading system message; the Mistral constraint only bans system-after-tool); (c) deliver rendered memory via the system/project-doc lane instead of a synthetic user turn. Compounding friction in the same trace: bbox_thread_list was deferred, so the task's one required tool cost an unknown-tool error + tool_search round-trip before work could start.
fallback_used: none — misattributed to model quality until the operator pushed back; events.jsonl forensics corrected it
notes: Provenance sharpened further: the blending is two deliberate mechanisms, not drift. (1) Memory-as-user-turn is an imported Codex idiom — agent_loop.rs ~651: absent --system-prompt ⇒ "Codex-style AGENTS.md discovery moves to UserInstructions in the contextual user message". Codex does this because OpenAI fixes their system/developer slot; we imported the workaround into a harness that OWNS its system slot, leaving it empty by default while standing rules masquerade as user speech. (2) The apply_ambient preamble is daemon lowest-common-denominator: prompt-string concat is the only surface the daemon controls for subprocess CLIs; in-process harness dispatches ride the same choke point even though the three-state --system-prompt channel exists and brofiles can already set it. Constraint to honor in the fix: Mistral 400s on system-after-tool, so MID-SESSION injections must stay user turns on openai-chat; session-START composition has no such excuse. Fix shape: at dispatch, route ambient/standing/rendered content into the system slot on harness transports (session start), keep prompt-concat only as the subprocess-CLI fallback, and reserve the user turn for what the operator actually said.
